propositions: Ruff ARG violations (unused parameters) across src/rebar total 64 instances (down from 72 post-retirement of bridge.py), spanning ARG001/ARG002/ARG005 rule families, and require systematic disposition without enabling a permanent gate.

Cluster-1 reconciler leaf handlers (10 sites in apply_inbound.py and apply_outbound.py) accept but never read client/repo_root parameters that are dispatched via string introspection in typed_dispatch.py, making naive _-prefixing unsafe at runtime.

Cluster-2 OutboundMapper Protocol implementations (7 sites across jira_datacenter/backend.py and jira_family/outbound_mapper.py) have keyword-pinned parameters governed by a Protocol contract and keyword call sites, so renaming breaks the interface.
RUF100 (unused-noqa) in pyproject.toml select blocks use of # noqa: ARG00x workarounds, forcing rename-unsafe parameters to remain as raw ARG violations rather than suppressed.
Three tracked real defects (timeout_s, close_reason, acli_cmd) are excluded from this sweep and left in place; no new defect-like accepted-then-dropped values are folded into mechanical fixes.

Post-sweep measured residual is 21 violations (64→21): 2 tracked-defect exclusions, 10 Cluster-1 normalized to **_kwargs, 7 Cluster-2 raw (no noqa possible), and 12 keyword/doc-pinned raw residuals; ARG gate remains disabled pending irreducible count review.
